definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese festival game where players try to scoop goldfish from a shallow pool using a thin paper scoop called a poi. A staple attraction at summer festivals.

examples.japanese: {夏祭|なつまつ}りで{金魚|きんぎょ}すくいをした。
examples.english: I played goldfish scooping at the summer festival.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{金魚|きんぎょ}すくいに{夢中|むちゅう}になっていた。
examples.english: The children were absorbed in goldfish scooping.

examples.japanese: {金魚|きんぎょ}すくいで{三匹|さんびき}も{取|と}れたのに、{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}にはもう{一匹|いっぴき}しかいなかった。
examples.english: I scooped three goldfish, but by the next day only one was left.

notes:
A beloved summer festival ({夏祭|なつまつ}り / {縁日|えんにち}) activity. Players pay a small fee and use a ポイ — a thin paper stretched over a wire frame — to try to scoop up {金魚|きんぎょ} from a shallow tub of water. The challenge is that the paper tears easily when wet.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {金魚|きんぎょ}すくいをする (to play goldfish scooping)
- {金魚|きんぎょ}すくいの{屋台|やたい} (goldfish scooping stall)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Goldfish scooped at festivals often don't survive long at home, which is a common shared experience in Japan. Professional {金魚|きんぎょ}すくい competitions also exist.
